clue.text: Page by titled woman about joint trailed by foremost of sleuths — her?

indicators.note: the sleuths' letter trails, coming after everything before it
the titled woman's word wraps about the joint, which sits just inside it

parts.note: a Dame is a woman holding the British title equivalent to a knighthood
J is slang for a cannabis joint

indicators.note: the foremost letter of the word sleuths is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzling biography: a page, a titled lady, something smoked, and the leading detective, all pointing at one mystery writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailed by' puts the S last. 'her?' only works as a definition with the rest of the clue: the whole clue describes the crime writer, herself a baroness, whose sleuth was Adam Dalgliesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points at a female crime novelist, made a life peer, whose books feature detectives; the question mark flags the indirect definition.

clue.text: Doctor in lead beginning to offer harmless drug

indicators.note: the doctoring word goes in the middle of lead's symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
to doctor a drink is to lace it, adding something to it

indicators.note: the beginning letter of offer is taken

explanation.surface: A physician, perhaps with lead in some potion, starts to prescribe a drug that does no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the physician who prescribes, but it is the verb meaning to lace.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill with no active ingredient is given for psychological effect, so it is a drug that cannot hurt.

clue.text: Judge to get rid of part of tournament?

parts.note: to oust is to get rid of or expel

explanation.surface: A judge decides to throw out part of a sporting tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval tournament was made up of mounted contests with lances, each one a single bout between knights.

clue.text: What poet did creatively maybe when consuming English cake

indicators.note: the poet's phrase swallows the letter for English, which ends up inside it

parts.note: a poet creating verse made a line, giving the two words MADE LINE

explanation.surface: A poet, perhaps, worked creatively while eating an English cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'maybe' signals that MADE LINE is just one example of what a poet might creatively do.
explanation.definitionFit: A small shell-shaped French sponge, famous from Proust, is a type of little cake.

clue.text: Common pedigree

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means ordinary, standard or commonplace, as in a ... phrase
... is lineage or ancestry, as in coming from good ...

explanation.surface: An ordinary lineage, a dog of mixed breeding perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as an adjective meaning standard or hackneyed and as a noun for ancestral line or breeding.

clue.text: Friendly fellow appearing in a yarn

indicators.note: the fellow's letter appears inside the phrase a yarn

parts.note: a yarn is a tale, and a fable is a kind of tale

explanation.surface: A friendly man turns up as a character in some story.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable describes someone genial and easy to talk to, so it is a synonym of friendly.

clue.text: Twitching antlers around last of these stags in watchful state

indicators.note: the jumbled antlers go around the final letters picked out
twitching suggests jerky movement, so the letters of antlers are jumbled
the last letters of these and of stags are taken

explanation.surface: Deer on alert twitch their antlers, watchful of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumble ALERTNS wraps the two final letters; 'stags' is not the definition but just supplies one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on guard and attentive is a condition of vigilance, a watchful state.

clue.text: Language from afar signified

indicators.note: the language is taken from within the run of letters of afar signified

explanation.surface: Meaning signalled in a tongue from a distant land.
explanation.definitionFit: Persian, the main tongue of Iran, is called by this name by its own speakers.

clue.text: Composer, amateur engaged by mischievous songwriter

parts.note: Bach is the German baroque composer

indicators.note: the amateur's letter is held, engaged, within the mischievous word

parts.note: arch means playfully mischievous, as in an arch look

explanation.surface: A composer, a mere amateur, gets hired by a cheeky songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer' looks like the definition, but it supplies only the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Burt Bacharach wrote many classic pop songs with Hal David, so he is a songwriter.

clue.text: Make time to take in French art that's serious

indicators.note: the make-plus-time letters take in the French word, which goes between them

parts.note: to make money is to earn it
es is French for (thou) art, the second person of the verb to be

explanation.surface: Find time to see some French art, which is serious stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is not painting but the archaic verb, 'thou art', which in French is 'tu es'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone earnest is sincere and grave in manner, which makes the word a synonym of serious.

clue.text: A place of pilgrimage containing court and leisure facility

indicators.note: the phrase a Rome contains the court within it

parts.note: Rome is a great destination for Catholic pilgrims
a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard of a college

explanation.surface: A pilgrimage site with its own courtyard and a leisure centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A purpose-built water sports centre, with a lake or pool for recreation, is a leisure facility.

clue.text: Feature again found in dire curriculum

indicators.note: the letters are found in the run of the words dire curriculum

explanation.surface: A topic keeps coming up in a terrible school syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen or appear once more, repeatedly, is to show up or feature again.

clue.text: One dumped by backward department getting praise

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, someone dumped

indicators.note: the department's name is read backward

parts.note: the Lot is a French département, named after its river

explanation.surface: Someone jilted by a backward civil service department nonetheless receives commendation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'department' means a French administrative region, here the Lot, not an office.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or glorify, so it is a verb synonym of praise.

clue.text: Sound of cat gathering in the end bird

indicators.note: the word for cat is said, giving the same sound with a different spelling

parts.note: kitty is a pet name for a cat
a wake is a gathering held at the end of a life, after a death

explanation.surface: A cat's noise draws a crowd, and finally a bird appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of cat' suggests a miaow, but it means the cat's word pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cliff-nesting gull named after its call is a kind of sea bird.

clue.text: Lout, I bet, upset close to austere place of incarceration

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
the close, the final letter, of austere is taken

explanation.surface: A yob bets that he will be thrown into a grim, bare cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon reached only through a trapdoor in the ceiling is a castle's place for imprisoning people.

clue.text: Money prohibited, we hear, for supplier of music?

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: we hear marks that the word for prohibited is said, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: banned means prohibited

explanation.surface: Cash outlawed, as rumour has it, for whoever provides music.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS for money is British slang, as in 'where there's muck there's brass'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble of horn and cornet players, as in a colliery group, plays tunes and so supplies music.

clue.text: Hobby Celt devised for dramatic character

indicators.note: devised means worked out or contrived, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A Celtic pastime is invented for a stage role.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Toby Belch is the carousing uncle of Olivia in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, a figure in a play.

clue.text: Fool detaining a name of stature

indicators.note: the fool's word holds, detains, the a and name letters

parts.note: git is British slang for a foolish or contemptible person

explanation.surface: An idiot holds back a big name with a reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of stature is a towering figure in a field, which is what the noun denotes figuratively.

clue.text: Island without area that is right for serving type

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the area letter is removed from the island

parts.note: Grenada is a Caribbean island
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An island without space, that is right for a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving type' suggests a waiter, but here it means a soldier serving in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of a Guards regiment, originally one who threw grenades, is a type serving in the forces.

clue.text: Frantic behaviour from notorious brothers cited

indicators.note: cited here means spoken out, so the brothers' name is pronounced to give a word with the same sound

parts.note: the Krays were twin gangsters who ruled London's East End in the 1960s

explanation.surface: Wild conduct by infamous siblings is quoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Krays, Ronnie and Reggie, were London's best-known criminal twins of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a mania or frenzy, short-lived wild enthusiasm, hence frantic behaviour.

clue.text: A good temperature in California is outstanding

indicators.note: the a, good and temperature letters go in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: pi is short for pious, which means good

explanation.surface: A pleasant warm spell in California is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old-fashioned adjective it means first-rate or splendid, so it equals outstanding.

clue.text: Earnestly sought religious area associated with revolutionary in plot

indicators.note: the religious area and the revolutionary go in the plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot, as in a flower bed
a see is a bishop's diocese
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A bishop, in league with a rebel in a conspiracy, made urgent pleas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a conspiracy, linking with 'revolutionary', but it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to implore or beg, so its past form means earnestly sought or begged for.

clue.text: Merit in Paris of introduction in court?

parts.note: de is French for of
in tennis the serve is the shot that starts each point on court

explanation.surface: Worth shown by a Parisian making a debut at a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a royal court or a courtroom; it is the tennis court, where a point begins with a serve.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to be worthy of it, which is what merit means as a verb.

clue.text: Steps person recalled in a slope being renovated

indicators.note: the recalled person goes in among the reworked letters
being renovated means being done up, so the letters of a slope are rearranged
recalled means called back, so the person's word runs backward

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a slope that is under repair, step by step.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters PASOLE are split after PASO to take the reversed person. 'Steps' looks like stairs, but means dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Latin ballroom dance modelled on a bullfight is a sequence of dance steps.

clue.text: Food store around hot place familiar to Indians

indicators.note: the food shop goes around the letter for hot

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A grocery shop near a spicy restaurant known to Indians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian capital city is somewhere well known to people from India.

clue.text: Green property entered by old diplomat

indicators.note: the envy word is entered by the old letter, which goes inside

parts.note: envy is the quality of being green, green-eyed with jealousy

explanation.surface: An estate in the countryside occupied by a former ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green property' suggests eco-friendly real estate; it is the property of being green with envy.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a messenger sent on a mission by a government, a type of diplomat.

clue.text: Orwell, maybe, sadly interrupted by institute

indicators.note: the sad word is broken into by the institute's letter

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sadly or unfortunately

explanation.surface: George Orwell, perhaps, sadly cut short by some institution.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair, so it is an example of an assumed name.

clue.text: Island with trade that's popular among Asians essentially

indicators.note: the trade word sits among the central letters picked out

parts.note: biz is the informal, popular word for business or trade, as in showbiz

clue.text: Comb sides of tower with pointed instrument

indicators.note: the sides, the outer letters, of tower are taken

parts.note: an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.definitionFit: To trawl is to search thoroughly, sifting through, as one combs an area for something.

clue.text: Noted chemist varies oil for analysis

indicators.note: analysis breaks something into parts, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous chemist tests different oils in his laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Lavoisier, the 18th-century Frenchman who named oxygen, is a renowned father of modern chemistry.

clue.text: Old actor is hard and boisterous

parts.note: Alan Ladd was a Hollywood star of the 1940s and 50s, such as in Shane
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A veteran actor is tough and rowdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddish describes rowdy, macho young-male behaviour, loud and unruly, hence boisterous.

clue.text: A German standing in for one in criminal court employment?

indicators.note: the a and German letters stand in for the one letter, replacing it

parts.note: a Yardie is a member of a Jamaican criminal gang
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A German replaces someone working at a criminal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal court' reads as one phrase, but 'criminal' is the gangster and 'court' belongs to the definition, a court being a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is the use of a yard for storage, so it is a cryptic description of using a courtyard.
